hypotheses.justification: Implied by hf and h. If b is a lower bound of f '' s, then for every x ∈ s, h gives f x - g x ≤ |f x - g x| ≤ C (abs_le), so g x ≥ f x - C ≥ b - C. Hence b - C is a lower bound of g '' s. The proof can build hg this way at the start and continue as written. (hf and hg can even be dropped together: if f '' s is not bounded below, the same argument shows g '' s is not either. Real.sInf_of_not_bddBelow then makes both infima 0, and the goal 0 ≤ C follows from h at a point of the nonempty s, since 0 ≤ |f x - g x| ≤ C.)
